Short answer
- Look for an LED, dimmable, adjustable task lamp with good efficacy (high lm/W), CRI ≥ 90, tunable color temperature (≈3000–5000 K), and an Energy Star or DLC listing. From your saved catalog I found a Meadowlight Lamp you could consider — but the product entry in memory has no technical details, so you'll need to verify its specs before buying.

Why an LED adjustable task lamp
- LEDs give much higher lumens per watt than incandescent/halogen and long lifetimes, so they’re the most energy-efficient choice for desk lighting.
- Dimming and color-temperature control let you use less power and tune light for task or comfort, improving perceived brightness without wasting energy.
Evidence: these are general, well-established points about LED vs. legacy lamps (industry-standard guidance). They are not pulled from the product catalog.

Catalog product found in memory
- Meadowlight Lamp — appears in the saved product catalog.
Evidence available in memory: the product name only. There are no stored spec sheets, provenance, or extractor data for Meadowlight Lamp, so I cannot confirm any performance or certification claims from the catalog entry.

What must be verified for Meadowlight Lamp (or any lamp before purchase)
- Light source: is it LED (vs. fluorescent/other)?
- Power consumption (watts) and lumen output (lm) — to compute efficacy (lm/W).
- Efficacy (lm/W) — look for ≥ ~80 lm/W for good efficiency; many modern LEDs are 100+ lm/W.
- Color rendering index (CRI) — CRI ≥ 90 is recommended for accurate color in offices.
- Tunable color temperature (CCT) range (e.g., 3000–5000 K).
- Dimmability and dimming method (smooth or with flicker).
- Certifications/listings: Energy Star or DesignLights Consortium (DLC) if you want certified efficiency.
- Standby/idle power draw (should be very low, e.g., <0.5 W).
- Lifetime (hours) and warranty.
- Mounting options (base, clamp) and adjustability to fit your workspace.
- Price and return policy.

Practical numeric targets to compare models
- Task lighting lumens: ~400–1000 lm depending on desk tasks and ambient light.
- Efficacy: ≥80 lm/W (better if ≥100 lm/W).
- CRI: ≥90 for color-critical work, ≥80 acceptable for general office.
- CCT: 3000–5000 K adjustable; 4000 K is neutral/office-friendly.
- Warranty: ≥2 years preferred.

Suggested next steps
- If you want, I can:
  - Pull the Meadowlight Lamp spec sheet (if it’s available in the catalog) and report exact wattage, lumens, CRI, CCT, certifications, and price.
  - Compare Meadowlight against 2–3 other energy-efficient desk lamps (I can search the wider catalog or public models).
- Tell me your priorities (budget, style, clamp vs. base, bright task vs. softer ambient) and I’ll make a short list with verifiable specs and a recommended pick.
